_readme: REGISTRY OF RETIRED CLAIMS — read tools/check-retired-claims.mjs for the full rationale.
When a certified essay retires an argument, that argument does not only live in the essay.
On 2026-07-29 a single retired Islam argument was found alive on SEVEN surfaces: the essay,
its mastery page, that page's flashcard deck, a quiz in daily-mix.html that GRADED readers on
it, two cards in worldviews.html, library/active-reading-data.json and daily-args.json. Each
was found only because something independent happened to look. This file makes that mechanical.
TO RETIRE A CLAIM: add an entry. `patterns` are case-insensitive regexes. `allow` lists files
where the string may legitimately appear — almost always because that page is the one DOING the
retiring (a page that says 'do not claim X' must be allowed to contain X). Keep `allow` as tight
as you can: a broad allow silently un-retires the claim.
`instead` is not decoration. It is what the next person needs in order to fix a hit correctly
rather than just deleting the sentence.

NETTING. Each claim declares `netting`: "claim" means the pattern is built from tokens + predication + tempered negation gaps and generalises across wordings; "phrase" means it is a literal blocklist that only catches the wordings someone happened to find. RULE: any claim retired on a FREE, INDEXED, deity/Trinity-tier surface must be claim-shaped. A phrase blocklist there reports green over live error -- that is not a hypothetical, it happened twice on 2026-07-29, the second time one day after the entry was written.

CORPUS. A claim-shaped entry carries `corpus.must_fire` / `corpus.must_not_fire`, and tests/content-integrity.test.mjs EXECUTES them. Recording test cases in a prose note is not a test: the quranic-title-compounds regex was mis-tuned five times, and every one of those mis-tunes would have been caught in one second by the cases already written down beside it. must_not_fire matters as much as must_fire -- a net that flags our own refutations gets ignored, which is how check-stamp-integrity reached 59 unread flags.

SOME ENTRIES SHOULD STAY `phrase`, DELIBERATELY. stoner-odds, nicaea-300-bishops, trinity-arithmetic-1x1x1, echad-composite-unity and objections-never-a-strawman are artefact-shaped -- the retired thing IS a token, so a literal net is the correct tool and rebuilding them would dilute the claim/phrase rule until it stops meaning anything. Entries that SHOULD be rebuilt carry a `rebuild_debt` field saying why and in what order.

claims.what: Arguing from the shared English word 'Word': the Qur'an is God's eternal Word, the Qur'an calls Jesus God's Word, therefore Jesus is eternal.
claims.why: It equivocates. The Qur'an's term for God's own speech is kalam (kalam nafsi in the Ash'ari resolution); Surah 4:171's term for Jesus is kalima. Sunni theology has never identified them, and a Muslim who knows the terms corrects it in one sentence. library/islam-eternalword.html disclaims this in its own Reply 3.
claims.instead: Run it structurally: settling the Mihna, mainstream Sunni orthodoxy held God's speech eternal and uncreated — 'neither He nor other than He' — and thereby built the very category it tells Christians is incoherent. Scope it to Ash'ari/Maturidi, not to Islam as such.
patterns: maps precisely onto the Christian claim
same Quran calls Jesus God's Word
Quran agrees that Jesus is a
the very parallel the text invites
the title carries eternal weight for a book
disagreeing only about whether that Word
claims.rebuild_debt: PHRASE-SHAPED ON A CLAIM-SHAPED SURFACE. This claim was retired on a free, indexed, deity/Trinity-tier surface (worldviews.html card 13, library/islam-eternalword.html), which the _readme rule says must be claim-shaped -- so the registry currently breaks its own rule in its first entry. Ten literal strings cover only the wordings someone happened to find; the distinctive MOVE (Qur'an-eternal-Word premise + Jesus-Word-title premise => shared eternity) has no general net. Known leak, verified by reading and NOT yet added as a must_fire because it would fail the suite before the rebuild lands: 'so the Muslim already believes in an uncreated Word - and his own book gives that title to Jesus' trips neither this entry nor quranic-title-compounds ('his own book' and 'that title' supply no Qur'an token, no Jesus token, no predicated title). REBUILD FIRST, then add that sentence as must_fire. Order after it: logos-distinct-from-essence (highest doctrinal stakes -- misses 'in some respect', 'somehow other than the essence', 'not wholly identical with the essence'), then ashari-formula-as-deity-predication ('neither Allah nor other than Allah' and 'not God and not other than God' both slip).

claims.what: Rendering the Ash'ari formula as 'neither God nor other than God'.
claims.why: The formula (la huwa wa la ghayruhu) is about the attribute vis-a-vis the ESSENCE, not a predication of deity. Rendered this way it predicates near-deity of an impersonal attribute, and when set beside John 1:1 it flattens the Son toward an attribute — the compressed-modalist direction.
claims.instead: 'neither He nor other than He' — neither identical with the bare essence nor a separate thing beside it. And state the asymmetry: the Ash'ari formula denies otherness; John positively confesses that the Word IS God, a divine person and not an attribute.
patterns: neither God nor other than God

claims.what: Attributing the QUALITATIVE reading of John 1:1c to Colwell's rule.
claims.why: Colwell (1933) was about DEFINITENESS. The qualitative analysis is Harner, Dixon and Wallace — and Wallace explicitly warns against this misapplication. ev-m-john11.html devotes a Hard objection to conceding that apologists overclaim Colwell.
claims.instead: Name the construction (anarthrous preverbal predicate nominative), attribute the qualitative force to Harner/Wallace/Harris, and note that verse 3 settles the matter independently of any grammar dispute.

claims.what: Claiming John 1:6, 1:12, 1:13 (or 1:18) are 'the identical construction' to John 1:1c, or that the NWT renders anarthrous theos 'God' THROUGHOUT John 1.
claims.why: Those are anarthrous genitives and accusatives, not preverbal predicate nominatives — there is no second instance in John 1. And at 1:18 the NWT prints 'the only-begotten god', lowercase, so 'throughout the chapter' is false. A well-read Witness has that verse ready. NOTE 2026-08-11: the original patterns were TOO NARROW and missed two live surfaces for 13 days - library/john11.html said "in numerous places the same construction is rendered God" (no quantifier match) and daily-mix.html said "elsewhere in the chapter" (not "in the same chapter"), the latter as the GRADED CORRECT ANSWER. Pattern 1 now catches the claim shape regardless of quantifier.
claims.instead: Say the NWT renders article-less theos as 'God' at 1:6, 1:12 and 1:13, explicitly warn that these are NOT the identical construction, and note 1:18 before the Witness does.
patterns: the same construction[^.]{0,40}(four times|in the same chapter|elsewhere in the chapter)

claims.what: Claiming Daniel's pelach ('serve') is used only of God, so Daniel 7:14 proves the Son of Man is divine.
claims.why: Daniel 3:12 uses it of Nebuchadnezzar's gods. ev-m-titles.html now concedes the verb is 'suggestive rather than decisive'. Widened 2026-08-11: the original five patterns matched none of 'receives worship', 'receives universal worship' or 'the worship of all nations', so the claim survived on daily-mix.html (as the GRADED CORRECT ANSWER), daily-args.json, ev-m-titles.html and pocket-cards.html. The ev-m-titles.html allow entry is now removed, not carried.
claims.instead: The clouds are the stronger half of the case — cloud-riding is YHWH's own vehicle in the OT. Treat the service-verb as suggestive, not decisive.
patterns: served with the (reverence|worship) due to God

claims.what: Claiming critics never argue the church invented the Son of Man sayings.
claims.why: The opposite of the record. Vielhauer, Perrin, Casey and Bultmann all argued versions of exactly that.
claims.instead: Say it is HARD to explain as a church invention — ~80 times on Jesus' lips, almost never in the epistles — and name the critics who do argue it.
patterns: critics never accuse the church of inventing

claims.what: Calling the Trinity 'the only formulation that keeps all the data'.
claims.why: Biblical unitarians and Oneness both claim to keep all the data. The page's own ARG_PREMISES was already calibrated to 'the most faithful reading, not a proof no thoughtful person could resist'.
claims.instead: The reading that keeps all the data at once, where every rival buys its simplicity by dropping a line of it.
patterns: only formulation that keeps all the data

claims.what: Presenting Bauckham's 'divine identity' category as recognised across scholarship.
claims.why: The category is contested. Hurtado read the same data as a pattern of devotion; James F. McGrath disputes the category outright.
claims.instead: 'widely influential, though the divine identity category is itself debated' — and name Hurtado and James F. McGrath (not bare 'McGrath', which reads as Alister).
claims.rebuild_debt: DO NOT PROMISE COVERAGE HERE. The overstated-consensus class is the least amenable to claim-netting: there is no fixed token, and 'recognised across scholarship' / 'universally accepted' / 'no serious scholar disputes' is an open set. This stays phrase-shaped on purpose. It is caught by reading -- by apologia-neutrality -- not by CI, and recording that here is better than leaving a false sense of coverage.

claims.what: Claiming the pre-Nicene doctrinal floor 'never moves', or that Arianism was expelled almost unanimously.
claims.why: Origen restricts prayer proper to the Father; Justin calls the Son heteros theos; Tertullian denies the Father-Son relation is eternal (Adv. Hermogenem 3). And the fifty years after Nicaea were a genuine fight — Homoian emperors held the field and Athanasius was exiled five times.
claims.instead: 'the floor that barely moves', name the wobbles, and note that the settlement was not secure until 381 — which is a better answer to 'won by the sword' anyway.

claims.what: Describing Latter-day Saints as living 'Christ-centred lives'.
claims.why: Concedes the object of worship, not merely the sincerity — and on this page's own account the Christ in view is a different Christ.
claims.instead: Concede sincerity and devoutness, then say plainly that sincerity is not the question at issue; who God is, is.

claims.what: The phrase 'underived aseity, possessed from the Father'.
claims.why: Self-cancelling as a standalone flashcard, and a compressed reader hears that the Son's self-existence was granted to him — derived deity.
claims.instead: 'the Son possesses the same underived, self-existent life, eternally from the Father' — with the fence: an eternal relation of origin, person from person, never a lesser or later deity.

claims.what: Saying in our own voice that the Logos is 'distinct in some way from the essence' or 'not simply identical to the essence'.
claims.why: That is the Arian direction. The orthodoxy gate rated it the nearest thing to a deploy-blocker in its batch.
claims.instead: One divine essence, undivided — eternally Father, Son and Spirit. Report Ash'ari attribute language as THEIRS, never as a description of the Logos.
patterns: distinct in some (way|sense) from the essence
not simply identical to the essence

claims.what: The promise that each objection is 'stated as its strongest defender would put it — never a strawman'.
claims.why: Measured against the essays' own ranking of the strongest objections, it was false on most mastery pages. A truth-in-labelling claim on a site whose named standard is 'Checked Before Published'.
claims.instead: 'Each objection is stated as you will actually meet it, then answered — with the hardest one named above and answered at length in the deep dive.'

claims.what: The round figure 'roughly 300 bishops' at Nicaea.
claims.why: The sources vary between about 250 and 318. The round number is a popular-apologetics artefact.
claims.instead: 'the sources vary between about 250 and 318 bishops'.

claims.what: Praising the Ash'ari resolution as 'a real/genuine intellectual accomplishment', 'a marvel of careful thought', or 'a model of theological seriousness'.
claims.why: Over-warmth toward a doctrinally rival position, and the essay's own 2026-07-14 stamp records removing exactly this. It survived in the FAQ, the JSON-LD schema and the worldviews card.
claims.instead: 'a serious and disciplined position' / 'serious theology, not evasion' — and always pivot immediately to what it concedes.

claims.what: Arguing that echad in the Shema means 'composite unity' and so hints at the Trinity.
claims.why: library/shema.html says honesty requires saying no: echad is the ordinary word for one and carries no such freight.
claims.instead: Run 1 Corinthians 8:6 as a deliberate reformulation of the Shema — noting that the reading is arguably dominant but genuinely contested (James McGrath).

claims.what: Stoner's probability figures for messianic prophecy (1 in 10^17 and similar).
claims.why: library/messianic-prophecy.html calls it pseudo-mathematics that should be retired: the probabilities are guesses multiplied as if independent.
claims.instead: Argue from textually secure prophecies (Isaiah 53:9) and from the Dead Sea Scrolls' pre-Christian dating, not from manufactured odds.

claims.what: Claiming the Isaiah 53 servant 'fits no nation'.
claims.why: Overstated, and it undercuts the page's own charity toward Judaism: the collective reading has a serious answer in the righteous remnant.
claims.instead: 'fits awkwardly with a purely collective reading, though its defenders answer with a righteous remnant'.

claims.what: Claiming classical writers preferred 1x1x1 to 1+1+1 as a Trinity illustration.
claims.why: No such source exists, and the arithmetic is vacuous.
claims.instead: State the contradiction charge properly — it must be 'X and not-X, in the same respect' — and meet the transitivity-of-identity argument rather than assuming it fails.

claims.what: Claiming as documented history — especially on the authority of 'the standard histories' — that the Mu'tazila pushed the created-Quran doctrine because they feared an uncreated Quran would vindicate the Christian doctrine of the uncreated Christ.
claims.why: The standard scholarly explanations of why al-Ma'mun imposed the Mihna are political and authority-based. Nawas 1994 — cited in library/islam-eternalword.html's own footnotes — reviews three current explanations and none of them is Christological. The claim traces to a single think-tank commentary, which worldviews.html then cited in its own 'Go deeper' list. Selling it as scholarly consensus is exactly the overstated-consensus defect the neutrality gate exists to catch.
claims.instead: Give the Mu'tazila's worry internally, which is well attested: anything genuinely eternal is uncaused and self-subsistent, and those are marks of deity, so an eternal Word beside God looked to them like shirk dressed in scripture. Christian writers under Muslim rule pressed the same structure from the other side (John of Damascus, before the Mihna crystallised the doctrine). Add the caution that the standard accounts of al-Ma'mun's motive turn on caliphal religious authority, and that nothing in the argument rests on the polemical motive.
patterns: vindicate the Christian doctrine of the uncreated Christ

claims.what: Presenting 'Kalimatullah' or 'Ruh Allah' / 'Ruh min Allah' as titles the Qur'an itself applies to Jesus.
claims.why: Surah 4:171 has kalimatuhu ('His word') and ruhun minhu ('a spirit from Him'); 3:45 has kalimatin minhu. The compounds are post-Quranic — Ruh Allah is pervasive in hadith, not in the Qur'an, and kalimat Allah at 9:40 is not about Jesus. A Muslim who knows the text corrects this in one line, which is the same failure mode as the NWT/John 1:18 error: a sentence that hands the other side an easy win inside our own argument. ROUND-4 LESSON: the first patterns here were written around the three specific phrasings found on one tier and missed the general form entirely, so CI reported green while worldviews.html's FREE, INDEXED tier still said the Quran calls Jesus 'the Word of God, the Spirit of God' -- contradicting the same card's own deep tier. Patterns must catch the Quran-attribution CONTEXT, not one wording. Do not widen to a bare 'the Word of God': that is the ordinary Christian title for Christ and the net would cry wolf on every page.
claims.instead: Say the Qur'an calls Jesus 'a word from Him' and 'a spirit from Him', and where the traditional title is worth naming, say plainly that Ruh Allah is a title Islamic tradition later drew from the verse rather than Quranic wording.

claims.note: ALLOW LIST IS EMPTY, and should stay that way. library/islam-preservation.html was carried as a debt for one round, then simply corrected (four words) -- closing a hole costs less than documenting it. Nothing is allow-listed: the guard exempts genuine refutations on merit rather than by filename, which is what keeps the net honest. TUNING HISTORY -- this entry was mis-tuned THREE times in one day, each time in a different way, so read before editing. (1) Patterns written around the three phrasings found on one tier: silent while the free indexed tier still ran the compound. (2) Rewritten verb-anchored (calls|names|gives): silent on 'affirms that Jesus is', 'calling Jesus', and a bare flashcard list -- three live survivals on ev-s6.html, flashcards.html and ev-m-trinity_islam.html. (3) Compound-anchored with a forward-only negation guard: fired on our OWN corrective ('Do not say the Quran calls Jesus Kalimatullah'), because the negation precedes the compound. The guard is now BIDIRECTIONAL -- negation up to 60 chars before OR after. Anchor on the compound (it is the retired artefact and cannot appear innocently); never widen to a bare 'the Word of God', which is the ordinary Christian title for Christ; and (4) Guard written with [^.<], which stops at an HTML tag -- so it could not reach the 'never' on the other side of an and fired on our own refutation again. The gap class is now [^.] (sentence-bounded, tag-permeable). Always test both directions AGAINST REAL MARKUP before committing -- a net that flags correct refutations gets ignored, which is how check-stamp-integrity reached 59 unread flags. (5) Pattern 2 was left forward-only and in one word order: it fired on 'the Quran never calls Jesus the Word of God' and was SILENT on 'Jesus, whom the Quran itself calls the Word of God' -- the exact phrasing then found live on library/islam-preservation.html. It now carries BOTH a sentence-level lookbehind and a verb-adjacent one, and handles the relative-clause order. Test set to preserve: it must fire on 'the Quran calls Jesus the Word of God' and on the whom-clause form, and stay silent on never/does not/do-not-say AND on 'the Quran itself is the Word of God', which is a true statement about the BOOK and must never be caught. (6) FOURTH mis-tune, and the last patch: the enumerated verb list could not see describes/refers to/identifies/is-called, had no 'Isa' (the word in card 04's own title), missed 'Word of Allah' entirely, and its negation guard had no 'nowhere' -- so it FIRED on the correct refutation 'The Qur'an nowhere calls Jesus the Word of God'. The verb list is now GONE: the pattern is Qur'an-token + Jesus-token + title adjacency, with TEMPERED gaps that may not themselves contain a negation (which is where 'nowhere' hid -- inside the match, invisible to both outer guards). Test corpus is 16 cases, both directions, and it must keep passing: it fires on describes/refers to/identifies/Isa/Word-of-Allah/is-the-Word forms, and stays silent on never/nowhere/does not/do-not-say/false, on 'the Quran itself is the Word of God' (true of the BOOK), and on 'For Islam the Quran is the Word of God. For Christianity, Jesus is the Word of God' (separate sentences, legitimate contrast). (7) Adjacency alone was still too loose: with no attribution link required it fired on our OWN essay's meta description, 'the parallel it opens to Christ, the eternal Word of God' -- orthodox confession, appositive, not a claim about the Qur'an. The title must now be PREDICATED of Jesus (an attribution verb or 'as' adjacent to the title, in either word order), not merely appositive to him. Corpus is 18 cases and both directions; keep it passing.

claims.what: Describing God's eternal speech as 'distinct from Allah yet divine' (or 'distinct from God yet divine').
claims.why: It inverts the Ash'ari formula, which DENIES that the Word is other than God (la huwa wa la ghayruhu). And predicating 'divine' of an attribute drifts toward treating it as a near-deity -- which, set beside the Son, flattens a divine person toward an attribute. Found live 2026-07-29 on ev-s6.html, in a script the reader is coached to say aloud.
claims.instead: 'neither He nor other than He' -- neither identical with the bare essence nor a separate thing beside it. Then state the asymmetry: the Ash'ari formula denies otherness; John positively confesses that the Word IS God, a divine person and not an attribute.

claims.what: Saying flatly that the Qur'an has Jesus predict his own death and resurrection (Surah 19:33).
claims.why: On the dominant Muslim reading 19:33 places the death in the future -- a natural death at the end of history -- and the raising at the GENERAL resurrection. So it is not a prediction of Jesus's resurrection in the sense a Christian reader will hear. Stated flatly it is corrected in one line. Found live 2026-07-29 on flashcards.html (the memorised layer) and in three worldviews.html headings/subtitles. REBUILT 2026-07-29 after the neutrality lens proved the first version was ALREADY LEAKING, one day after it was written, on the very file it was created to clean: worldviews.html said 'The parallel with the Christian account of the resurrection is impossible to miss' and neither literal pattern could see it. The two phrasings it did carry were simply the ones that happened to be found. It is now token + verb + object with tempered negation gaps, and it requires a Qur'an anchor -- without one it would fire on the true and orthodox Christian statement that Jesus predicted his own resurrection. Axis gaps closed 2026-07-29 (neutrality): the object alternation missed 'raised alive', which is the CARD'S OWN phrase for 19:33, and the verb axis missed prophesy/announces/foresees. Two escape tokens were also removed from the negation gaps -- 'verbal' and 'shared form' are topic words lifted from our own then-current sentence, not negations, so they made the net pass on that sentence rather than on the general property. Negation gaps must contain negations.
claims.instead: 'speaks of his own death and being raised (19:33) -- though the dominant Muslim reading places both in the future, at a natural death and the general resurrection.'

claims.what: Contrasting Christianity's love for the undeserving with Islam's account of divine love -- 'our God loves sinners before they deserve it, theirs does not'. Retired from worldviews.html card 14 in three places: premise 7's Romans 5:8 coda, Pro section 3's 'sinners who have earned nothing', and the gracious close's third parallel clause.
claims.why: The contrast LOSES, and it loses to a doctrine Islam states in its own voice.
